chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb al-Kulaynī, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, who said:
I wrote to ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام: A man set aside something from his wealth for you—may Allah make me your ransom—then he came to need it. Should he take it for himself, or send it to you?
So he said: He has the choice in that so long as he has not removed it from his hand. And if it reached us, we would consider consoling and assisting him with it, since he has come to need it.

He said: And I wrote to him: A man bequeathed to you—may Allah make me your ransom—some specified part of his wealth, and he also made a bequest to his relatives from his father's and mother's side. Then he changed the will, depriving those whom he had given and giving to those whom he had deprived. Is that permissible for him?
So he wrote عليه السلام: He has the choice in all of that until death comes to him.

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest or will
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death, marking the end of his discretion
key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: having legal discretion or choice in the matter

ai.seo_question: Can a person take back wealth set aside for the Imam or change his will before death?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding property set aside for the Imam and the changing of a bequest before death. It establishes that a person retains discretion over such property and over his will as long as it has not been transferred and death has not yet come.
